Important cohort distinction: the 458 original rows are from the no-person parquet. The 11 added original printer photographs visibly contain people and were freshly captioned by assistant visual inspection. They are a printer-targeted supplement, not a random sample. Combined percentages therefore describe this collection, not HP's product or environment distribution. The original parquet and its captions are unchanged.
1. Every device family 2. Products & environments3. Supporting surfaces 4. Surrounding objects5. Product/environment associations 6. SCAP patterns for every group7. Method & downloads

1. The same breakdown for every device family

Each device has its own role, environment, support, material, surrounding-object and nine-field SCAP statistics, including every observed device/environment combination. Primary and secondary appearances are included. One image can therefore contribute to several device sections.

Supports belong to the device being counted, not automatically to the scene's focal product. Reviewed focal-product placements are preserved; other devices require an explicit device-specific caption relationship. Unknown relationships remain unknown. Multiple explicit placements within one device family are multi-label image-presence counts. Surrounding-object tables exclude that device's own entity family; SCAP tables describe the whole scene.

6. SCAP patterns for every product & environment group

Every profile below is on this page. Each contains all nine SCAP fields, normalized pattern counts, and up to six repeated 2-4-word phrases. Phrase counts describe caption wording, not additional visual facts. n=1 is a single observation, not a recurring pattern; n=2-4 is sparse and descriptive only. Larger groups can still contain related shots of the same scene. Added visual captions and original Qwen captions have different authoring styles.

7. Method, limitations & downloads

Original source: s3://foundry-hp-enterprise-adobe-assets/parquets/hp_lifestyle_noperson_t2i_20261025_v1.0.0.parquet. All 458 rows are retained: 432 train and 26 validation; 160 lifestyle_hp_brand and 298 lifestyle. There are 457 augmented images and one real image according to source metadata. The baseline has 215 unnamed product records.

Printer supplement: 11 unmatched original identities out of 15 reference photographs. The four already represented identities were not added again. All 11 additions contain physical people. The source originals were visually inspected and freshly captioned by the assistant; no new Qwen, GPT or Gemini batch-caption run is claimed. The industrial-machine identification uses the source catalog and is kept separate from desktop printers.

Counting: image-presence counts use each image once per category. Primary focus and environment are exclusive assignments; device, object, material and field tags are multi-label. Tables show their denominators. Source scene variants remain distinct image identities, including similar office photographs; 469 unique identities do not mean 469 independent scenes. No product-model identity is inferred from appearance.

Evidence: the original 458-row analysis is caption-derived with reviewed heuristic normalization, not an independent visual assessment of every baseline image. Every device family now has a device-specific support audit: reviewed focal placements, explicit device-entity placements, or supporting furniture that explicitly names the device. Another product's desk is never used merely because it occurs in the same scene. Printer placements retain the earlier reviewed coding. Two baseline captions directly claim physical-person presence (a lap and a distant person); these are caption warnings, not newly verified visual findings. Screen/poster depictions are not counted as physical people. Unknown support/material remains unknown.

SCAP coverage: all nine fields are nonempty in all 469 records. Field tags are rule-based and non-exhaustive; an absent tag means no normalized match, not visual absence. Repeated phrases require at least two images and can reflect template wording. Exact field values are retained in downloads.

For product-shot generation: use product-specific support and environment associations as descriptive guidance, not engineering specifications. This analysis supplies no measured clearances, validated physical dimensions, or tested generation success rates. People visible in added references are not recommendations to introduce people into a no-person output.
